commit_subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 generalize (PR #1300): decouples component gates from exemplar flags; PR body says the witness's exemplar coupling "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins" — logic/scope correction to 100 merged generated modules.
description: never again zeroed by China-list or aluminum membership (the witness's exemplar coupling, which round-2 evaluation showed unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins)

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The §122 temporary-import-surcharge exemption branch fired on the witness's exemplar line flags (`if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0`), so it zeroed the 10% surcharge for every China-301-listed line regardless of origin and tied the genuine §232 carve-out to one aluminum exemplar row, whereas the cited proclamation excludes only the Annex I/II product categories and articles subject to §232 restrictions.
triage.triage_notes: Reference module for this chunk; read the full diff plus pre-fix and post-fix file windows. Provision WAS read: resolve_provision.py on us/rulemaking/federal-register/2026-02-25/2026-03824 (resolution_mode axiom_encode_resolver, fix_time_corpus_match same_body) shows the §122 surcharge exclusions are product categories (a)-(l), including '(k) all articles and parts of articles currently or that later become subject to additional import restrictions imposed pursuant to section 232' — §301 list membership is not an exclusion, confirming the pre-fix branch had no source basis. Attempted us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-230 as well but the pinned release resolves that path to §232 steel TRQ notes, not the cited aluminum/steel/copper exception text, so pagination differs; not load-bearing. Multi-rule fix: besides §122 it re-grounds section_201_component_rate (entry_is_line_e -> entry_is_section_201_cspv; both branches are 0 so no runtime change, expired safeguard), section_232_aluminum_component_rate (entry_is_line_b -> entry_is_section_232_aluminum, both versions), china_section_301_component_rate (4 of 5 slots re-gated to per-list membership), and brazil_/forced_labor_section_301_component_rate (drops the untraceable `if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0` suppression and ADDS the missing list-membership requirement — that sub-change is closer to unrepresented_clause). Kind could alternatively be argued as wrong_entity_or_scope (exemption applied to the wrong population); I chose untraceable_branch because the exemplar flags have no counterpart in the source at all and the fix re-grounds rather than re-scopes them. The commit also ADDS a new §232 steel component (ch13_s232_steel_heading_rate = 0.50 and section_232_steel_component_rate, summed into schedule_statutory_stack) — new coverage rather than a corrected value, so it is not the defect I scored. Decoupling is partial by design: entry_is_line_d survives in the §338/beer path and in one China-301 slot, and `if origin_is_brazil and not entry_is_line_b` survives untouched in the IEEPA reciprocal component. Note a9562cfd44 is an INTERMEDIATE commit of PR #1300, not its merge: the added section_232_steel_component_rate here carries a malformed double-nested `metadata.proof.proof.atoms`, repaired later in a14f43975 'b1.6: repair the steel proof chain per review finding' (the PR issue comment describes that repair plus two masked defects).
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as a rename or a generator-level refactor and could not: `entry_is_line_a` maps to two different semantic inputs in two different rules (`entry_is_section_122_exempt` in §122, `entry_is_china_301_list123` in §301), so it is a semantic split of an overloaded proxy flag, not a one-to-one rename, and encoded outputs change (the PR enumerates 18 witness-slice cells that changed because "the witness's own coupling was the unlawful part"). The rule's own proof atoms are byte-identical pre and post and already ground versions[1] on "subdivision (aa)(ii) exclusion list under heading 9903.03.03" plus "articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper or derivative aluminum or steel articles provided for in headings 9903.82.02 and 9903.82.04" — so the encoding claimed one exemption scope and implemented a different predicate. Reading the cited provision through the pinned release (Proclamation 11012, FR 2026-03824 ¶14) confirms the surcharge "shall not apply to the following products, as further detailed in Annexes I and II", items (a)–(m) including (k) articles "subject to additional import restrictions imposed pursuant to section 232" — nothing in the source makes §301 list membership or a specific exemplar HTS row the exemption trigger. That is a branch condition with no basis in the cited source which the fix re-grounds, i.e. untraceable_branch, not unrepresented_clause (the exemption branch already existed) and not wrong_entity_or_scope (entity, period, dtype and output surface are unchanged).
triage.verifier_quote:
-      (((((((if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0
+      (((((((if entry_is_section_122_exempt or entry_is_section_232_covered: 0
triage.verifier_notes:
Bundle: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maxghenis-TheAxiomFoundation-axiom-encode--claude-worktrees-zealous-heyrovsky-31a96b/86103d8f-b97f-4559-a96c-7e79bdbe616d/scratchpad/inputs/us/a9562cfd44.json; diff: .../scratchpad/diffs/us/a9562cfd44/012.diff.

One caveat a reviewer should see: the first reader's stated mechanism ("zeroed the surcharge for every China-301-listed line regardless of origin") matches the PR body and the pre-fix module summary ("entry_is_line_a ... are caller inputs supplied by entry preparation from incidence classification"), but the shipped parent-commit entry-prep tool populates those flags as literal exemplar rows: `git -C /Users/maxghenis/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us show 29dbbdac05:tools/b16_entry_flags.py` has `WITNESS_LINES = {"entry_is_line_a": "7202111000", "entry_is_line_b": "7601103000", ...}` and `result = {name: hts == digits for name, digits in WITNESS_LINES.items()}`. Under that literal wiring the ch13 defect is the mirror image — neither witness row occurs in chapter 13, so the §122 exemption never fired there and every Annex I/II and §232-covered ch13 line was charged the full 10%. Either wiring makes the pre-fix condition an ungrounded proxy for the proclamation's stated exclusion scope, so the kind is unchanged, but the reader's specific over-suppression narrative is the PR's account, not something I could reproduce from the parent-commit tool.

The diff is multi-defect and the reader picked the strongest anchor. Two other rules in the same file carry a different kind: `brazil_section_301_component_rate` and `forced_labor_section_301_component_rate` previously applied their rates to every entry of the listed origins with no listedness gate (`elif origin_is_brazil: brazil_section_301_additional_duty_rate`), and the fix adds `entry_is_brazil_301_listed and` / `entry_is_forced_labor_301_listed and` — that slice reads as unrepresented_clause. The new `section_232_steel_component_rate` + `ch13_s232_steel_heading_rate` and the extra `+ section_232_steel_component_rate` term in `schedule_statutory_stack` are new coverage the module never claimed (PR: "a Section 232 steel component the witness never had"), so they are an enhancement, not a defect, and should not be counted as a second finding. Note also that both post-fix Brazil/forced-labor inputs are hard-defaulted FALSE in `tools/b16_entry_flags.py` ("Follow-up incidence tables are not yet entry-preparable"), so those components evaluate to 0 in practice; that does not affect the §122 finding.

Supporting source text (pinned release us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap, corpus commit e79781bdde, provision sha256 c85d073b98bb...): ¶14 "I determine that the surcharge imposed in this proclamation shall not apply to the following products, as further detailed in Annexes I and II to this proclamation" with (k) "all articles and parts of articles currently or that later become subject to additional import restrictions imposed pursuant to section 232".
